newsitem.title: ITALY: Policeman arrested in Naples Mafia probe.
newsitem.headline: Policeman arrested in Naples Mafia probe.

text.p: The former head of the drug squad in the southern Italian port of Naples was arrested on Friday on suspicion of collusion with organised crime, police said.

Costanzo Sossio, who headed the squad for 10 years, was arrested as part of a probe into alleged connections between police officers and the Camorra, the local equivalent of the Sicilian Mafia, police said in a statement.
The probe made headlines last week when 19 officers were arrested in Naples on suspicion of dealings with the Camorra.
National police chief Fernando Masone said in a separate statement that Sossio, who was recently appointed police chief of the town of San Giuseppe Vesuviano near Naples, had been suspended.
Sossio, 46, faces charges of calumny, arms trafficking and falsification of documents.
"It's an unfortunate and tough situation, but we won't let it get us down," Naples police chief Luciano Rosini told reporters.
"We have faith in the magistrates and we are certain that they are working in the best way possible. These episodes only strengthen our will to work better," he added.
